decisions.decision: Merge Phase 209 despite a red Linux Full Suite
decisions.rationale: The single failure was verified failing-node-SET-identical on the branch's own merge-base be3cff54 — the same node, same message — so the branch introduced zero new failures. Only 'Windows Sensor Smoke' is a required check and it passed. A count comparison would have looked identical while proving nothing; the SET comparison is what justified the merge.

decisions.decision: Fix task 17's presentation string but NOT the metric
decisions.rationale: scan_error_rate is a scoring input (scoring.py:483 weight 6.0, :490 weight 5.0). Recomputing it moves the emitted score — the counterfactual at the true 1.1% is 18/100 rather than 15/100. Four days before a client demo, changing a displayed sentence is a different risk class from changing a scored quantity. Verified byte-identical afterwards.

decisions.decision: Align config.yaml's output.directory to quirk-output rather than the other way
decisions.rationale: The chaos lab bind-mounts ../quirk-output to /out and multihost-scan-config.yaml writes to /out, so lab scans already land there — the directory db_path had already called canonical. Moving db_path instead would have broken the lab.

decisions.decision: Fix the missing PDF in the Dockerfile, not just the running container
decisions.rationale: The docker exec fix was ephemeral — one `compose down` and PDF rendering silently disappears again mid-demo. It also fixes the SHIPPED sensor image for every user, since any containerised deployment had the same silent gap.

decisions.decision: The master guide is GENERATED, never hand-merged
decisions.rationale: A hand-merged master is stale the moment anyone edits a source, leaving two contradictory descriptions of the same behaviour — the exact drift class this session's reconciliation existed to remove. Deriving it means the master cannot DISAGREE with its sources, only lag them, and the lag is one command wide. It also preserves the five sources as canonical, so CLAUDE.md's doc checklist and the Obsidian sync table need no changes.

decisions.decision: Keep the [identity] exclusion but correct its stated reason
decisions.rationale: The reason was falsified — pyOpenSSL 26 requires cryptography<47,>=46.0.0, a floor not a cap; cryptography resolved to 46.0.6; pip check clean; a live scan enumerated X25519MLKEM768, the capability the doc said was lost. But the exclusion is still a defensible conservative default and a CI test guards it. Deleting the wrong claim was rejected in favour of quoting it in the correction: a wrong claim that silently disappears cannot be learned from.

decisions.decision: Record the six doc-audit false positives rather than discarding them
decisions.rationale: Every one looked like real drift: '5.5.7' was an OID fragment, '5.3.1' a section number, `quirk hardware` hits were NEGATIVE references saying the command does not exist, and a reported '76 undocumented config fields' was purely an extractor artifact. Without the record the next audit re-finds all six and spends the same time disproving them.

decisions.decision: Split the reconciliation fixes across two PRs
decisions.rationale: Four were mechanical find-and-replace; three required a judgment call (softening a documented safety instruction, choosing where security env vars belong, writing a conceptual section that did not exist). Mixing them would have buried the three that deserve real review under four that do not.

blocking_constraints.name: Exit code is not evidence
blocking_constraints.discovered: Three separate live failures on 2026-09-16, each exiting 0
blocking_constraints.mitigation: Assert the observable outcome, never the exit code: a launched browser, a file with %PDF magic bytes, an HTTP 200 carrying a non-empty body of the right type. scripts/validate-fresh-install.sh is built entirely on this principle.

blocking_constraints.name: A count produced by the audited tool is not a measurement
blocking_constraints.discovered: Six doc-audit false positives, including a '76 undocumented config fields' figure that was entirely an extractor artifact
blocking_constraints.mitigation: Re-derive every count with a second, independent method before recording it. Disagreement between the two IS the finding.

blocking_constraints.name: A self-check that exercises only the skip path proves nothing
blocking_constraints.discovered: validate-fresh-install.sh --self-check passed while skipping all nine checks
blocking_constraints.mitigation: Mutation-test the guard. Break the thing it watches and confirm the test goes red. Used on both the install script's harness and the master-guide fence tracker (breaking the tracker kills 4 of 11 tests).

blocking_constraints.name: zsh does not word-split unquoted parameter expansions
blocking_constraints.discovered: pytest $sel passed 53 paths as ONE argument and ran zero tests, reporting '2 warnings in 0.00s' which tails like a clean run
blocking_constraints.mitigation: Use ${=sel}, and confirm the summary reports an 'N passed' count rather than only warnings.
